### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**8** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/system.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/system.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3b8c724cf21fe2b39b2c635c6ef2a2448fa952fb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e3df4241ec7d2cb22c1d0c7f71df344dc06b7253` — the merge of head `38faba5a6070b5bccd419d6327ef406d1de80dc9` into base `3b8c724cf21fe2b39b2c635c6ef2a2448fa952fb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e3df4241ec7d2cb22c1d0c7f71df344dc06b7253 && git checkout e3df4241ec7d2cb22c1d0c7f71df344dc06b7253
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3b8c724cf21fe2b39b2c635c6ef2a2448fa952fb 38faba5a6070b5bccd419d6327ef406d1de80dc9 && git checkout -B drift-repro 3b8c724cf21fe2b39b2c635c6ef2a2448fa952fb && git merge --no-ff 38faba5a6070b5bccd419d6327ef406d1de80dc9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3b8c724cf21fe2b39b2c635c6ef2a2448fa952fb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

The seat's in-thread orders (keep the better-auth option; re-aim `assertPasswordResetEndsSessions` instead of deleting it; no D2) were judged as rulings the tree must satisfy, not as findings.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes the diff implies, each judged against the tree:

1. `EmailAndPasswordConfigSchema.revokeSessionsOnPasswordReset` goes from `z.boolean().optional()` to `retiredKey(REVOKE_SESSIONS_ON_PASSWORD_RESET_RETIRED)` (auth-config.zod.ts:342). Per `shared/retired-key.ts` that is a `z.never` with the guidance as its error map, made `.optional()` and described `[REMOVED] ...`: absence and `undefined` pass, every other value is refused with the prescription on both channels (tsc via the never-typed input, the parse via the error map). RIGHT: this is exactly the removal the ruling 「一律吊销,不加开关」 and the card's "retire the key with a tombstone" ask for, and nothing else in the schema moves.
2. `AuthConfigSchema` inherits the refusal at `emailAndPassword.revokeSessionsOnPasswordReset` (the nested path pin in the new test). RIGHT, derived, no extra code.
3. New public export `REVOKE_SESSIONS_ON_PASSWORD_RESET_RETIRED` from `@objectstack/spec/system` (`system/index.ts:73` re-exports `auth-config.zod`); api-surface/system.json and export-origins/system.json carry the one new row. RIGHT: a widening of the export surface only, by one string constant, so that plugin-auth and the schema say the same prescription; it is not a widening of what a configuration may hold, so `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is not contradicted (the narrowing face judges the accept set).
4. authorable-surface/system.json row becomes `system/EmailAndPasswordConfig:revokeSessionsOnPasswordReset [RETIRED]`; the `authorable-surface.base.json` row stays unannotated, which is correct, that file is the pinned anchor at `baseRev`, not the live surface (its own description says so, and `AccessControlConfig:maxAge` shows the same pair of readings). RIGHT.
5. `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR[18]` gains `system/EmailAndPasswordConfig:revokeSessionsOnPasswordReset` via the entries file; the filename `18.system__EmailAndPasswordConfig__revokeSessionsOnPasswordReset.ts` is the README's derivation of the id (`/` and `:` to `__`), the value matches the authorable-surface row minus `[RETIRED]`, the spelling gate (b) in build-schemas reads. RIGHT.
6. D3 semantic entry `email-and-password-revoke-sessions-on-reset-retired` under `entries/semantic/18.*.ts`, no `conversionIds`, non-empty `reason` and `acceptanceCriteria`; `STEP18_RATIONALE` fragment with the same id, `order: 118` (one more than the highest existing, 117), inserted where the id sorts (between `element-text-variant-heading-subheading-retired` and `email-template-category-is-system-retired`), which is what `packages/spec/scripts/step18-rationale-merge.test.ts` pins (sorted unique kebab ids, positive integer order, NEXT_ORDER = max+1). RIGHT.
7. No D2 conversion. Judged against the tree rather than the PR body: `AuthConfigSchema` is consumed by nothing in `packages/spec/src` outside its own file (grep), `stack.zod.ts` has no key holding it, and plugin-auth's `AuthManagerOptions`, which extends a partial of `AuthConfig` (auth-manager.ts:669), is the only consumer, i.e. the configuration a host hands the plugin in code. Nothing `os migrate meta` could rewrite exists, so the `AccessControlConfig.maxAge` / `EnhancedApiError.fieldErrors` precedent (D3 only) applies, and the prescription rightly carries no `os migrate meta` sentence (the class pin `retired-key-migrate-sentence.test.ts` judges only prescriptions that name the command). RIGHT, and it matches the seat's ruling.
8. plugin-auth: `assertPasswordResetEndsSessions` now takes `unknown` and refuses the key at any defined value (`!== undefined`) with `[auth] ` + the spec prescription; it ran before and runs now at the constructor (auth-manager.ts:1613) and on the merged block in `applyConfigPatch` (auth-manager.ts:2090). The premise that it is reachable holds: no file in plugin-auth parses through `AuthConfigSchema` (grep: only three comments mention it; `one-time-token-handoff.ts:198` states the manager receives plain objects). The function is not exported from the package index, so its signature change is not a public-surface change. RIGHT, and it is the seat's re-aim order, not the card's delete order, carried out.
9. `auth-manager-auth-instance.ts:392` keeps better-auth's own `revokeSessionsOnPasswordReset: true`, set unconditionally and never read from `this.config`, so the behaviour the ruling fixes is unchanged; `auth-manager.test.ts:2074` now pins that better-auth still receives `true` with no host key. RIGHT, per the seat's ruling.
10. The `externalVocabulary` example comment (auth-config.zod.ts:321-326) no longer cites the retired key and names five live siblings forwarded by name; checked against auth-manager-auth-instance.ts:357-389, all five are forwarded under their own name (`disableSignUp` and `requireEmailVerification` as resolved values). RIGHT. Note, not a finding: `enabled` and `resetPasswordTokenExpiresIn` are forwarded by name too and are not in the list; the list is illustrative and the old comment omitted them as well.
11. Docs: HARDENING.md (two sites, both updated), content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx:313 (a producer the card did not list, now says the key is retired and refused at any value), generated content/docs/references/system/auth-config.mdx (two `[REMOVED]` rows, the generator's tombstone rendering). `content/docs/releases/` untouched, as required. No skill teaches the key (0 hits in `skills/` at base and head). RIGHT.
12. Re-check `git grep -n revokeSessionsOnPasswordReset -- packages docs skills content` at the head: every remaining hit is the tombstone, the exported prescription, the plugin guard and its tests, the better-auth option, generated references, the registry entries, the retirement pin, the anchor base.json, and released CHANGELOGs. No producer writes the key. Card acceptance "no producer anywhere writes the key" holds.
13. Liveness: no `packages/spec/liveness/*.json` row names `EmailAndPasswordConfig` (grep over `packages/`), so there is no ledger row to re-grade; the `Spec property liveness` check-run on the head concluded success. RIGHT.

Dogfood pinned to the head (the narrowing face's order): the CI `Dogfood Regression Gate` check-run on this head concluded success, but that is the aggregator over a matrix that `ci.yml:2395` skips on `pull_request` by design (`github.event_name != 'pull_request'`), so CI has NOT run the battery on this head. The only dogfood reading pinned to `d217dd5f` is the dev's `os-verify-lock: VERDICT command-exit 0` (414 files / 3427 tests, 47m35s). It names this head, and the chronology fits (head committed 17:21:51Z, report stamped 18:15Z, a 47m35s run in between). This review is read-only and cannot re-measure it; the seat accepts it as the dev's pinned claim, which is what the order asked for, and a push run on main will run the matrix.

Check-runs on the head at the second reading: concluded success: Auto Label, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate (aggregator, see above), Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, PR-body guards, Plan Test Core shards, Spec property liveness, filter. Skipped by design: 18.x upgrade harness, Dogfood Regression Gate matrix, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Schedule gate, Temporal Conformance, UI Published Artifacts. Still pending (in_progress): Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Check Changeset, Lint · CI release and engine gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs and code guards, Lint · repo and tooling gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup and corpus, Live E2E UI, Test Core 1/8 through 8/8, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · workspace. The verdict below is on what has concluded plus the tree; the pending families (notably Check Changeset, the Type Check set, and Test Core, which run the retirement pin and the plugin-auth refusals) must conclude green before landing, and a red among them re-opens this record.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/29909-revoke-sessions-on-password-reset-retired.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth: minor`, BREAKING banner, FROM to TO remedy ("Delete the key; nothing replaces it"), marker `adr-0087: registered email-and-password-revoke-sessions-on-reset-retired`. Judged against the tree: the id resolves to the new D3 entry at the head and is new in this diff, which is what `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` requires of `registered`; `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` grades a declared `(narrowing)` arm as a BREAKING change that ships `minor` during the launch window (line 1839), so `minor` on both packages is the grade the gate expects, and `major` would be refused. The precedent #29827 changeset graded plugin-auth `patch` for its narrower narrowing; `minor` here is the conservative side and is what the grader names. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` on the PR body and the changeset agree with each other and with the diff: the accept set of a published schema key shrinks to absence, no package publishes anything new except the one prescription constant, which exists to carry the narrowing's own message. Level matches the diff.

Clause-②: no (narrowing). What is taken away, measured at the consumer: (a) a typed or parsed auth configuration may no longer carry `emailAndPassword.revokeSessionsOnPasswordReset` at any value; (b) plugin-auth no longer accepts `true` at the key (it accepted `true` and refused `false` since #29827). Both are the key itself leaving, which is what 「一律吊销,不加开关」 and the card's "retire the key" remove, and nothing beyond it: the better-auth option stays set, every reset door still ends every session, the revocation trail is unchanged, an absent key is accepted as before. Nothing is widened.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report `open_questions: []`. Nothing to answer.
- Dev report `out_of_scope_findings`: the overlap check read open PR text only, not file lists. Judged here: the four `hits` files are new or touched only by this PR; `registry.ts.template` is the one shared file, and the fragment is inserted in its own sort gap, which is the merge-safe shape the template's header prescribes. Not a blocker; noted for the seat's land-time rebase.
- Dev flag "assertPasswordResetEndsSessions is NOT unreachable" (falsifies the card's delete clause): confirmed against the tree (① item 8). The seat's re-aim ruling is what the tree implements. Answered.
- Dev flag "no forward of the spec key in auth-manager-auth-instance.ts": confirmed; the literal at :392 is written, never read from the host config, and the absence walk excludes that one file with the reason beside it. Answered.
- Dev flag "HARDENING.md had two references, not three": confirmed by the diff (row 263 and the step-3 comment). Answered.
- Dev flag "no liveness ledger row": confirmed (① item 13). Answered.
- Card acceptance "`check:authorable-surface`, `check:generated` and the liveness ledger are green": liveness concluded green on the head; authorable-surface and generated artifacts are the dev's local readings (all 14 up to date after the origin/main merge) and ride in the pending `Lint` / `Build` families. Escalated to the pending check-runs, not to a person.
- Nothing in this PR touches a Tier H surface; the Governed Surface Queue Guard concluded success.

### ④ Design judgment

Per `hits` file, each tried against the code it cites and the scenario it is accepted against:

**packages/spec/src/system/auth-config.zod.ts**: against the ruling and its first consumer (plugin-auth). The tombstone is the helper's canonical form; the prescription follows the skill's five conventions (backticked qualified key first; `was removed in @objectstack/spec 18 (ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove)`; a dash clause saying why; "Delete the key" plus the mechanism now in force; no migrate sentence because no conversion covers it) and carries no tracker number (the pin asserts this). Exporting the prescription so that the plugin's refusal is byte-identical is the right call: a host that never parses through the schema would otherwise meet a second wording. Tried to break it: an explicit `undefined` passes both the schema and the guard (consistent, and the pin's CONTROL covers it); `null`, `0`, `'false'`, `{}` are refused by both (pinned on both sides); the walked shape keeps the key so the `[RETIRED]` row and gate (c)'s ageing clock work. The `externalVocabulary` comment now makes a true claim. Holds. No finding.

**packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/retired-keys/18.system__EmailAndPasswordConfig__revokeSessionsOnPasswordReset.ts**: against `entries/README.md` and gate (b). Filename derived from the id, `export const entry` with the exact `defKey:name` string, the comment above it is what lands in the generated table and says why the key went and where its D3 lives. Holds. No finding.

**packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.email-and-password-revoke-sessions-on-reset-retired.ts**: against `SemanticMigration` and the upgrade-guide reader. Id matches the filename, the changeset marker and the rationale fragment; `replacement` tells the author what to do and what now holds; `reason` names the one judgment no tool can make (a deployment-maintained writer of the key); `acceptanceCriteria` is verifiable (boots without the key; a second-device session answers 401 after a reset). No `conversionIds`, correctly, and the pin asserts no D2 names the key. Should-fix (low): `surface` reads `auth emailAndPassword.revokeSessionsOnPasswordReset — whether …`, a space where the author path has a dot and a trailing explanatory clause; the sibling `18.audience-posture-default-invite-only.ts` spells its surface as the plain dotted path (`system.AuthConfig.audience`) and the skill says to write the surface the way an author writes the key. Nothing matches on it, so this is readability of the printed guide only; spell it `auth.emailAndPassword.revokeSessionsOnPasswordReset` and move the gloss into `reason` if wanted. Not a FAIL.

**packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template**: against `step18-rationale-merge.test.ts` and `joinRationale`. One fragment, id equal to the D3 id, `order: 118` = highest + 1, inserted at the id's sort position, text with no leading or trailing space and sentences that read correctly joined after its neighbours (it opens with "It also retires …", the house form). Holds. No finding.

Narrowing itself against the published spec on `main`: on `main` the key is `z.boolean().optional()` and plugin-auth accepts `true`. At the head the key is unwritable and the plugin refuses it at any value. The capability taken away is the declaration of a setting that had one legal value, which is what the ruling removes; the behaviour (always revoke) is untouched, and the spec's own refusal is made real at the one door the schema cannot reach (an unparsed host object), with the same text. Nothing the ruling keeps is removed.

Must-fix: none.
Should-fix: the D3 `surface` spelling (above).
